Alex/Priya — thanks for the call today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. Please correct anything I missed.

Summary of pain points (as discussed)
- Intermittent latency spikes during payroll cut windows (~2x baseline traffic for ~90s).
- Current provider shows unstable p99s when sequence length >256 tokens.
- Need strong data isolation (VPC + audit logs) for PCI-adjacent flows.

Goals (30/60/90):
- 30d: proof-of-concept handling baseline traffic with p95 < 120ms for 256 tokens.
- 60d: scale to peak bursts (350–400 QPS) with p99 < 450ms and automated fallback behavior.
- 90d: GA plan for dedicated capacity across us-west/us-east with warm pools and runbook.

Model & quality constraints:
- Primary model candidates: openwizard-13B (preferred quality) + fallback openwizard-7B.
- Need deterministic output for snippets used in reconciliation; we discussed sampling/temperature guardrails.

Initial technical asks from ZenithPay (to confirm)
- Share a 7-day sample of QPS by minute and typical request token distributions (attachment: zenithpay_qps_sample.csv).
- Confirmation that VPC private deployment is available and timeline for audit log export.
- Work with your infra team to validate a small dedicated spike environment for a 2-week trial.

Proposed next steps
1) ZenPay to send QPS sample + representative prompt set (action: ZenithPay).
2) Redwood SE (Marissa) to draft a deployment sketch and recommended instance profile (action: Redwood; by EOD 29 Sep).
3) Schedule a 90-minute technical workshop (ops + infra) — propose Thu 2 Sep (I mean Thu 2 Oct) from 10:30–12:00 PT.

Attachments: zenithpay_qps_sample.csv (csv)

Thanks — Rishi

Rishi — thanks for the quick recap, that matches our notes. A few clarifications / additional constraints from our side:

Traffic profile details
- Baseline: ~120 QPS (auth flows + UX).
- Payroll peaks: nominally 380 QPS sustained ~2–3 minutes; historical peaks up to 550 QPS for <30s during settlement windows.
- Token distribution: 60% < 128 tokens, 30% 128–512, 10% >512 (mostly reconciliation summaries).

Latency & routing expectations
- p95 target for interactive flows: <120ms.
- p99SLA for reconciliation endpoints: <500ms — tolerance for occasional 10% windows where we accept degraded throughput but must not drop requests.

Security/compliance
- VPC peering is mandatory for the trial; we also need audit log retention for 90 days initially.
- We will need to validate key rotation workflow with your security team.

Infra contact
- Looping in Samantha (CloudOps) to coordinate network peering and estimate runway for dedicated GPU capacity in our accounts.

Attachments: sample-p99.csv (p99 by endpoint)

Happy to proceed with the 90-minute workshop — Thu 2 Oct works for Priya and me.

Best,
Alex

Alex / Priya / Samantha — thanks, looping in a technical sketch and recommendations based on the traffic profile you shared. This is intended as an SE-level starting point for the workshop.

High-level deployment topology (recommended)
- Dedicated GPU pools in two regions: us-west (primary) + us-east (secondary) behind a smart router.
  - Primary pool: 4 x H100 (latency-critical) + 8 x A10G (cost-efficient throughput).
  - Secondary pool: 6 x A10G for failover and burst handling.
- Routing: policy-based routing with token-aware batching. Reconciliation endpoints pinned to H100 pool; interactive endpoints served from mixed pool with KV cache.

Autoscaling & warm pools
- Warm pool target: maintain warm instances to cover 60% of expected peak (i.e., ~330 QPS headroom). Warm-start strategy: pre-load KV caches during off-peak + keep one H100 reserved for instant warm-up.
- Scale triggers: sustained 60s avg QPS increase of >20% OR p95 > 120ms for 3 consecutive 1-min windows.

Batching & latency control
- Continuous batching with latency cap of 80ms for interactive flows (decay to per-request pass-through if cap breached).
- Separate batching queues by token-length bucket (0–128 / 129–512 / >512) to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Model considerations & fallbacks
- Primary: openwizard-13B quantized (4-bit) on H100 for p95 goals.
- Fallback: openwizard-7B quantized on A10G if burst > threshold or p99 degrades; route reconciliation to smaller model only for non-critical batch windows.
- Warm cache policy: preserve KV for frequently used prompt prefixes during payroll windows.

Observability & SLOs
- Instrument per-route p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, batch size distribution, and queue latency.
- SLA proposal (draft): p95 < 120ms (interactive), p99 < 500ms (reconciliation), 99.9% availability for dedicated pool.

Security & operations notes
- VPC peering + IAM roles for log export: Redwood can export audit logs to your S3/GCS bucket; rotation tested via staged key rotation.
- We will run a short security questionnaire before the trial; provide point person and required controls.

Attachments included with this note:
- deployment_sketch_v1.pdf (deployment diagram + sizing)
- qps_projections.xlsx (projected QPS by hour for trial)
- infra_topology.png (network peering sketch)

Quick ask list before workshop
1) Full minute-level QPS sample for last 30 days (if available).
2) A small set of representative prompts for reconciliation that we can use for latency benchmarking.
3) Contact for security questionnaire (for log retention and key management).

Quotation / cost note (high level)
- We will price the 2-week spike environment as a reserved short-term pool; SE will share numbers after workshop once we validate instance mix.
